investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes do not match the pod's affinity or selector at all, making preemption ineffective. As a result, every remote agent pod creation attempt stalls as Unschedulable for ~143–149 seconds before the eval times out, and no VM identity or state is ever returned to the runner. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is localized to this observability eval.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the runner received no response payload, so orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState were never written.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the agent creation call never completing.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduling error message, latencyMs=154905, empty evidenceKeys — all three checks in the remote-agents feature share the same infrastructure failure.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which triggers the pod scheduling path that is failing.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots on the nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector are currently consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, and those 2 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm quota. If the affinity rules are overly narrow (e.g., targeting a specific node label that only 2 nodes carry), relaxing them could expose additional schedulable nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for peak load: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the cluster may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus live workloads, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.

Lower confidence — a recent infrastructure change reduced the number of nodes carrying the required node label or reduced the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota per node, but no infrastructure change evidence is present in the supplied packet to support this directly.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval succeeds and returns non-empty evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in ['running','idle','ready']), the exhaustion was transient and self-resolved, disproving a persistent capacity deficit.

If cluster inspection shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and unused on the two affinity-matching nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but rather a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, quota policy, or admission webhook rejection).

Add a remote-agent-create latency trend eval that tracks pod scheduling time across runs and warns when the unscheduled duration approaches the outage threshold (360000ms), enabling proactive capacity intervention.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 2026-07-04T15:34:08Z and 2026-07-04T15:39:08Z with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, and consequently none of the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were written, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to schedule a new remote agent pod. At the time of the eval run, both kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes were fully allocated (0/2 available), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. This prevented the eval's createAgent call from completing, so the probe exited with a scheduling-timeout failure message before any evidence could be collected, causing all four required evidence fields to be missing and the expected-output contract to be violated entirely. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: both nodes that carry this extended resource were fully allocated at eval time, leaving no capacity for a new remote agent pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

CONTRIBUTING — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already constrained to 2 nodes before resource limits are applied. Even if kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity were restored, a future capacity spike could re-trigger this if the affinity pool is not expanded.

SECONDARY — no preemption victims available: the scheduler attempted preemption on the 2 eligible nodes and found no lower-priority pods to evict, indicating the nodes are occupied by pods of equal or higher priority. This rules out a simple priority misconfiguration as a quick fix.

UNLIKELY — eval runner token or org resolution failure: the runner checks for args.token before proceeding (run-status-probes.mjs line 1902) and would return a SKIP status, not a scheduling error message, if the token were absent. The observed failure message is a Kubernetes scheduler event, not a SKIP, so token absence is not the cause.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out (~148–149 s) before the scheduler can place the pod. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool; it is not a code defect in the eval runner or the expected-output contract. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence — leaving all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes do not match the pod's affinity or selector at all, making preemption ineffective. As a result, every remote agent pod creation attempt stalls as Unschedulable for ~143–149 seconds before the eval times out, and no VM identity or state is ever returned to the runner. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure, not an eval runner or contract configuration defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; the impact is localized to this observability eval.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 149s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=155504 — the eval ran for ~155s, well past the pod's 149s unscheduled window, confirming the pod never became ready before the check ended.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the runner received no response payload, so orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState were never written.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, consistent with the agent creation call never completing.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same scheduling error message, latencyMs=145625, empty evidenceKeys — confirms the failure is not isolated to the create check.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduling error message, latencyMs=154905, empty evidenceKeys — all three checks in the remote-agents feature share the same infrastructure failure.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which triggers the pod scheduling path that is failing.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots on the nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector are currently consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, and those 2 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm quota. If the affinity rules are overly narrow (e.g., targeting a specific node label that only 2 nodes carry), relaxing them could expose additional schedulable nodes.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for peak load: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the cluster may be insufficient for concurrent eval runs plus live workloads, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.

Lower confidence — a recent infrastructure change reduced the number of nodes carrying the required node label or reduced the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota per node, but no infrastructure change evidence is present in the supplied packet to support this directly.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval succeeds and returns non-empty evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent=true, remoteState in ['running','idle','ready']), the exhaustion was transient and self-resolved, disproving a persistent capacity deficit.

If cluster inspection shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and unused on the two affinity-matching nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but rather a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, quota policy, or admission webhook rejection).

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector is found to match more than 2 of the 6 nodes, the '4 node(s) didn't match' message would indicate a label drift on those nodes rather than an intentionally narrow affinity rule.

If only remote-agent-create failed while remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime passed in the same run window, the failure would be isolated to the create path rather than a shared infrastructure constraint — but the current evidence shows all three failed.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested ratio on affinity-eligible nodes and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing earlier signal before full exhaustion causes pod scheduling failures.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the remote agent pod's affinity/selector rules match at least a minimum number of healthy nodes (e.g., >= 3), catching label drift or misconfiguration before it reduces the schedulable pool to an insufficient size.

Add a remote-agent-create latency trend eval that tracks pod scheduling time across runs and warns when the unscheduled duration approaches the outage threshold (360000ms), enabling proactive capacity intervention.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out (~148–149 s) before the scheduler can place the pod. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool; it is not a code defect in the eval runner or the expected-output contract. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or real workloads have consumed all available VM quota, leaving no capacity for new scheduling attempts.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node selector or affinity rules, reducing the effective scheduling pool to only the 2 already-saturated peer-pod nodes.
Tertiary — peer-pod VM quota is correctly sized but a prior eval run's cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs) failed to release VM resources, causing quota to accumulate across runs.

Lower probability — the kata peer-pod provider (e.g., cloud VM quota, peerpod-controller) hit an external limit that prevented new VMs from being registered as available on the 2 capable nodes, making them appear saturated even if pod slots were nominally free.

If VM slots are genuinely exhausted by real workloads, consider scaling up the peer-pod-capable node pool or increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on existing nodes to restore eval and provisioning capacity.

Review the eval runner's cleanup path (withCleanup in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) to ensure remote-agent pods and their VM resources are reliably released after each probe run, preventing quota accumulation across scheduled eval cycles.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available and unused on the 2 peer-pod nodes at the time of the eval run, the resource-exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or API failure would need to be investigated.

If the 4 affinity-excluded nodes were found to have been recently reconfigured to support kata peer-pods and the pod's node selector was stale/incorrect, the primary cause would shift to a node affinity misconfiguration rather than resource exhaustion.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient scheduling race or a brief quota spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed in a subsequent run, the shared VM pool exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a check-specific issue would need to be investigated.

If the eval runner logs showed the probe exiting via the 'No access token configured' early-return path (run-status-probes.mjs line 1915) rather than a scheduling error, the root cause would be a missing token rather than a Kubernetes scheduling failure.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' status rather than a scheduling timeout failure.
Add a VM slot leak detection eval that periodically lists all pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and alerts if any have been running beyond the expected eval cleanup window.

Add a node affinity/selector validation eval that verifies the remote-agent pod spec's node selector matches at least one Ready node in the cluster, catching affinity drift before it causes scheduling failures.

Consider a synthetic eval that measures the time-to-schedule for a minimal kata peer-pod (without full agent initialization) to isolate scheduling latency from agent startup latency in future failures.
